From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@mediushealth.com>

Cc: procurement@mediushealth.com

Subject: Request: SLA addendum and order form language for Medius Health

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement and our infra team ran through Redwood’s baseline SLA and asked whether we can add a short, customer-specific addendum to the MSA that includes:

- An uptime commitment of 99.95% per calendar month for the hosted API endpoints used in production (excluding scheduled maintenance with 48h notice).
- A latency SLO for P95 text-generation calls of <300ms within the US region for standard request sizes (up to 1024 tokens).
- A credit regime for breaches (pro-rated credit % tied to downtime minutes).
- Explicit fallback/rollover behavior if a region is degraded (automatic routing to alternate region with advertised latency impact).

We will need redlineable language to attach to our MSA and an order form reflecting committed capacity (Dedicated / reserved GPUs) and monthly fees. Procurement asked for the addendum + order form to be shared by COB Tuesday so legal can run it through our internal review before the exec approval meeting next Friday.

For context: Medius is planning to go-live with a customer-facing recommendation feature in Q4 and we need predictable latency and a path for credits if the target SLOs are missed.

Attached is our standard SLA request template (doc) to help you map terms to our procurement fields.

Attachments: [Medius_SLA_Request_Template.docx]

Can you confirm you can provide a draft addendum and a matching order form by Tuesday? Also flag any items that would require a scope exception (e.g., on-prem/private deployments or data residency).

Thanks —
Sofia Ramos

Laura / Karthik —

Forwarding Sofia’s template and our initial reply. Procurement wants a redlineable addendum + order form by Tuesday COB. Key asks from Medius:

- Uptime: 99.95% per calendar month (they will want explicit exclusions and scheduled maintenance notice window).
- Latency: P95 < 300ms (US region) for requests up to 1024 tokens.
- Credits: pro-rated credits tied to cumulative downtime minutes, capped at 50% of one monthly committed fee; credits are Redwood's exclusive monetary remedy.
- Failover: automatic routing to alternate region if primary region is degraded — they want explicit language describing expected latency degradation and a communication protocol.

Notes for legal: we should flag the following exception points that may require negotiation or signoff from ops:
1) The P95 <300ms on hosted API may only be achievable with Dedicated/reserved capacity for sustained workloads above N TPS — suggest we map latency SLOs to capacity commitments on the order form (e.g., reserved vCPU/GPU tiers).
2) Maintenance window: we typically give 48h notice for planned maintenance; with Dedicated customers we can offer narrower windows but need SOC/ops approval.
3) Credits regime: propose a cap at 50% of one month’s fees for catastrophic events; need to confirm with finance.

Karthik — can you validate whether the 1024-token bucket is the right bound and supply a short paragraph we can include saying: “For P95 latency guarantees, Redwood will provide monitoring and a remediation plan tied to committed capacity; if capacity is increased by the customer, latency guarantees will be re-evaluated.”

Laura — can you draft redlines that: a) incorporate the uptime/latency language, b) clarify exclusions and remedies, and c) include a statement that credits are exclusive remedy unless otherwise agreed in the SOW. Also add a placeholder for the order form capacity commitments.

Target: draft back to customer + order form by Tue 2026-05-05 COB.

Thanks —
Ben

Hi Sofia —

Thanks for the heads-up and the template. Attached are two documents: a redlineable SLA addendum and a matching order form that maps the latency SLO to reserved capacity. Major points we included:

- Uptime: 99.95% monthly uptime commitment with defined exclusions (force majeure, customer-caused events, scheduled maintenance with >=48h notice).
- Latency: we included a P95 <300ms target in the US region conditioned on the customer selecting the "Dedicated-Standard" capacity tier on the order form (Order Form section 2.1).
- Credits: pro-rated credits tied to cumulative downtime minutes, capped at 50% of one monthly committed fee; credits are Redwood's exclusive monetary remedy.
- Failover behavior: described automatic routing to an alternate region with an expected latency delta note; included notification and runbook steps.

We flagged a few negotiation points in redline:
1) If Medius insists on P95 guarantees for hosted (non-dedicated) usage, that will require an exception and an ops SLA review — this is non-standard.
2) Any lower credit cap or removal of the credit cap requires director-level sign-off from Finance.

I’ve attached: Redwood_SLA_Addendum_draft_v3.pdf (redline-enabled) and Order_Form_Medius_2026-05.docx. If this looks right, Ben — please send to Sofia/Procurement with the DocuSign link for execution.
